headline: 991 children dead as measles outbreak worsens in Bangladesh
summary: Four more children died in 24 hours, with 917 new infections reported by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
details: Four children died within the last 24 hours due to measles and measles-like symptoms, according to the latest report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The total death toll from measles and related symptoms has reached 991 children since March 15, with 100 of these deaths being laboratory-confirmed cases of measles.
In the last 24 hours alone, 917 children were infected, including 74 confirmed cases and 843 showing symptoms. During this period, 761 children were admitted to hospitals, while 571 were discharged.
The outbreak began early this year, but critics and analysts say government efforts to prevent it were severely lacking from the start.
Reports indicate that vaccination efforts were neglected during the interim government's tenure last year, contributing to the current severe outbreak.
While a mass vaccination campaign was conducted from April to May, over 3.9 million children were missed, allowing the infection to continue spreading.
Since March 15, a total of 163,105 children have shown measles symptoms, and 19,641 have been confirmed as positive. A total of 143,214 patients have been hospitalized.
Analysts warn that the scale of deaths and the daily infection rate seen this year are unprecedented in the history of measles outbreaks in Bangladesh.
caption:
991 children have died in a devastating measles outbreak across Bangladesh. 4 more died in just 24 hours.

Four children died within the last 24 hours due to measles and measles-like symptoms, according to the latest report from the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

The total death toll from measles and related symptoms has reached 991 children since March 15, with 100 of these deaths being laboratory-confirmed cases of measles.

In the last 24 hours alone, 917 children were infected, including 74 confirmed cases and 843 showing symptoms. During this period, 761 children were admitted to hospitals, while 571 were discharged.

The outbreak began early this year, but critics and analysts say government efforts to prevent it were severely lacking from the start.

Reports indicate that vaccination efforts were neglected during the interim government's tenure last year, contributing to the current severe outbreak.

While a mass vaccination campaign was conducted from April to May, over 3.9 million children were missed, allowing the infection to continue spreading.

Since March 15, a total of 163,105 children have shown measles symptoms, and 19,641 have been confirmed as positive. A total of 143,214 patients have been hospitalized.

Analysts warn that the scale of deaths and the daily infection rate seen this year are unprecedented in the history of measles outbreaks in Bangladesh.

headline_marked: Fuel crisis: [[Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expresses regret]] over shortages
headline: Fuel crisis: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expresses regret over shortages
summary: The PM identified the fuel crisis as the country's biggest current problem and stated that an action plan is already in place to resolve it.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed his regret to those suffering from the ongoing fuel crisis in Bangladesh. He described the fuel shortage as the country's most significant problem at the moment.
Speaking at a discussion meeting on Saturday (September 5) marking the 48th anniversary of the BNP, he stated that an action plan has been developed to solve the crisis.
The Prime Minister also warned that some groups are spreading confusion regarding the problems of the autocratic era and the interim period, stating that action will be taken against any anarchy.
He urged everyone to stay within their limits and called on BNP activists to work diligently to ensure that citizens do not suffer.
Tarique Rahman further claimed that while the BNP remained active on the streets, some groups operated in secret during the autocratic regime and are now revealing themselves.
He called for the transparency of those who were hiding during the previous regime, suggesting that some may still be attempting to create anarchy from the shadows.
The Prime Minister reaffirmed that the BNP government will implement all promises made to the people to build a democratic and prosperous Bangladesh.
caption:
The fuel crisis is now the country's biggest problem. Prime Minister Tarique Rahman says an action plan is in place to fix it.

Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expressed his regret to those suffering from the ongoing fuel crisis in Bangladesh. He described the fuel shortage as the country's most significant problem at the moment.

Speaking at a discussion meeting on Saturday (September 5) marking the 48th anniversary of the BNP, he stated that an action plan has been developed to solve the crisis.

The Prime Minister also warned that some groups are spreading confusion regarding the problems of the autocratic era and the interim period, stating that action will be taken against any anarchy.

He urged everyone to stay within their limits and called on BNP activists to work diligently to ensure that citizens do not suffer.

Tarique Rahman further claimed that while the BNP remained active on the streets, some groups operated in secret during the autocratic regime and are now revealing themselves.

He called for the transparency of those who were hiding during the previous regime, suggesting that some may still be attempting to create anarchy from the shadows.

The Prime Minister reaffirmed that the BNP government will implement all promises made to the people to build a democratic and prosperous Bangladesh.
